settings.accounts.addAccount.description: Button in Settings → Accounts & Connections (HI-2107): adds an account (asks which coding agent CLI, its name and where it gets its model), then opens its sign-in or sets up its server. It comes with its first connection.

settings.accounts.addConnection.description: Button under an account's connections (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): adds a connection on it (a dialog).

settings.accounts.affected.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {# running agent runs on another connection than the one chosen for it now.} other {# running agents run on another connection than the one chosen for them now.}}
settings.accounts.affected.description: Banner in Settings → Accounts & Connections after a connection was turned off or the default changed (HI-1755): how many running agents are on a connection other than the one chosen now.

settings.accounts.changeFailed.description: An error's title: renaming a connection, turning it on or off, or making it the default failed.

settings.accounts.changedTo.description: A warning on a connection (Settings → Accounts & Connections): its login changed (a /login typed in a pane). {now} and {was} are emails.

settings.accounts.checkedAt.description: The tooltip of a connection's state (Settings → Accounts & Connections): when it was last checked. {when} is how long ago ("5 min ago").

settings.accounts.closeRunningConfirm.description: The confirm button of that dialog: ends the CLI and hides its terminal.

settings.accounts.closeRunningMessage.defaultMessage: {cli} is still running in it. Closing the terminal ends it.
settings.accounts.closeRunningMessage.description: The message of that dialog ({cli}: the coding agent CLI, "Codex"): closing ends the CLI and what it started.

settings.accounts.closeRunningTitle.description: Title of the dialog asked by Close under a connection's sign-in or Set Up terminal while the CLI in it still runs (Settings → Accounts & Connections).

settings.accounts.closeTerminal.description: Button under a connection's sign-in or Set Up terminal (Settings → Accounts & Connections): hides it, ending the CLI in it if it still runs (asks first then).

settings.accounts.connection.base.description: A mark on an account's first connection (HI-2107): the one a new agent on that account gets first. Keep it short.

settings.accounts.connection.baseTip.defaultMessage: The first of its account: what a new agent gets when this account is first in the order and on here.
settings.accounts.connection.baseTip.description: The tooltip of "First" on a connection (HI-2107).

settings.accounts.connection.duplicate.description: An entry of a connection's ⋯ menu: adds a copy of it, named "<name> (2)".

settings.accounts.connection.edit.description: An entry of a connection's ⋯ menu (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): opens its dialog.

settings.accounts.connection.failed.description: An error's title: duplicating or removing a connection failed (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107).

settings.accounts.connection.remove.description: An entry of a connection's ⋯ menu: removes it (asks first; refused while something uses it).

settings.accounts.connection.removeMessa.defaultMessage: Only this setup goes: its account and its other connections stay.
settings.accounts.connection.removeMessa.description: The message of the dialog confirming a connection's removal (HI-2107).

settings.accounts.connection.removeTitle.description: Title of the dialog confirming a connection's removal ({name}, its name; HI-2107).

settings.accounts.copilotAs.description: GitHub Copilot's account (HI-2107): who its PC-wide sign-in is ({account}, a GitHub user name).

settings.accounts.copilotNotSignedIn.defaultMessage: Not signed in: sign in from Provider Setup
settings.accounts.copilotNotSignedIn.description: GitHub Copilot's account when it isn't signed in (HI-2107). Provider Setup names a dialog.

settings.accounts.defaults.failed.description: An error's title (Settings → Accounts & Connections; HI-1770): saving a connection's default model, effort or context failed.

settings.accounts.keep.description: Button on a connection whose login changed (Settings → Accounts & Connections): takes on the login it is now signed in as.

settings.accounts.keepFailed.description: An error's title: Keep the New Login failed.

settings.accounts.keepRename.description: After Keep the New Login on a connection ({name}): offers to rename it, since it is now another login.

settings.accounts.leftover.defaultMessage: Not all removed: {what}. Remove tries again; nothing outside its folder was touched.
settings.accounts.leftover.description: A warning on a connection (Settings → Accounts & Connections) whose removal stopped partway. {what} is what's left, in English.

settings.accounts.list.desc.defaultMessage: Add an account (signed in, or a server) and the connections agents choose on it, and turn accounts on in this workspace. Drag accounts into your order: a new agent gets the first connection of the first account that's on here.
settings.accounts.list.desc.description: What the list "Accounts & Connections" does, under its title (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107: one order of accounts for every coding agent CLI; a new agent gets the first connection of the first account on in the workspace).

settings.accounts.list.tip.defaultMessage: A sign-in account is a folder of its own that Combwork made, signed in with the CLI's own sign-in in your browser: Combwork never sees or keeps its login. Its conversations and memory are shared with your other accounts through a link to the CLI's projects folder. Removing an account deletes its folder and its login on this PC, never your conversations. GitHub Copilot signs in once for the whole PC, in Provider Setup: its account is that sign-in.
settings.accounts.list.tip.description: The info tip of the list "Accounts & Connections" (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): more on what it does and when it applies. Provider Setup names a dialog.

settings.accounts.list.title.description: A setting's title (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): the list of accounts, each with its connections.

settings.accounts.loading.description: Settings → Accounts & Connections while its list loads.

settings.accounts.more.description: The ⋯ button of an account or a connection (Settings → Accounts & Connections), for screen readers and its tooltip ({name}, its name).

settings.accounts.moreProjects.description: The last item of that list when it names only the first projects: how many more there are.

settings.accounts.moveAccount.defaultMessage: Drag to change the order of {name}, or press Alt+Up or Alt+Down
settings.accounts.moveAccount.description: The tooltip and label of an account's drag handle (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): it moves the account in the one order of accounts. Alt+Up and Alt+Down name keys.

settings.accounts.moveFailed.description: An error's title: moving a connection in its coding agent CLI's order failed (Settings → Accounts & Connections).

settings.accounts.name.description: The label of the box for a connection's name (Settings → Accounts & Connections).

settings.accounts.needName.description: Under the name box of a connection (Settings → Accounts & Connections) while it's empty.

settings.accounts.noWorkspace2.defaultMessage: Open a workspace to choose which accounts are on in it.
settings.accounts.noWorkspace2.description: Settings → Accounts & Connections with no workspace open: whether an account is on is per workspace (HI-2107).

settings.accounts.noneYet.defaultMessage: No accounts yet. Add one, then sign it in.
settings.accounts.noneYet.description: Settings → Accounts & Connections when there are no accounts (HI-2107).

settings.accounts.notTrusted.defaultMessage: Not trusted yet in this workspace: {projects}
settings.accounts.notTrusted.description: Under a connection that needs set up (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-1870): the projects of the open workspace whose folders its coding agent CLI hasn't been told to trust yet ({projects}: their names, listed). Set Up asks the CLI's trust question for each in turn.

settings.accounts.notice.context.defaultMessage: Use 200K context: {value} (its CLI has no such choice)
settings.accounts.notice.context.description: A moved setting in the notice (Settings → Accounts & Connections; HI-1770): a context choice the agent's CLI doesn't have, kept on the agent but not used. {value} is On or Off.

settings.accounts.notice.dismiss.description: Button (Settings → Accounts & Connections; HI-1770): hides the notice of moved settings for good.

settings.accounts.notice.effort.description: A moved setting in the notice (Settings → Accounts & Connections; HI-1770): an effort level ({value}) the agent's model doesn't offer, kept on the agent but not used.

settings.accounts.notice.hint2.defaultMessage: They weren't carried over. To use one, choose or make a connection with it for the agent.
settings.accounts.notice.hint2.description: Under the notice of moved settings a connection can't use (Settings → Accounts & Connections; HI-1770, HI-2107): those values aren't part of the agent's connection.

settings.accounts.notice.line.description: A line of the notice of moved settings a connection can't use (Settings → Accounts & Connections; HI-1770): the project, the agent and the setting with its value ("Effort: high").

settings.accounts.notice.model.description: A moved setting in the notice (Settings → Accounts & Connections; HI-1770): a model, kept on the agent.

settings.accounts.notice.title.defaultMessage: Some settings moved onto agents can't be used by their connection
settings.accounts.notice.title.description: A notice's title (Settings → Accounts & Connections; HI-1770): a project's own model, effort or context settings were moved onto its agents (connections hold the defaults now), and some of them the agent's connection can't use: they are kept on the agent but not used.

settings.accounts.onHere.description: The switch on a connection (Settings → Accounts & Connections): whether it is on in the open workspace.

settings.accounts.onHereShort.description: The switch on an account (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): whether it is on in the open workspace. Keep it short.

settings.accounts.plan.description: A connection's identity in Settings → Accounts & Connections: the email it is signed in as, and its plan as the CLI names it ("max").

settings.accounts.providerSetup.description: The only entry of GitHub Copilot's account's ⋯ menu (HI-2107): opens the Provider Setup dialog, where its sign-in is.

settings.accounts.remove.description: Button on a connection (Settings → Accounts & Connections): removes it and deletes its folder (asks first).

settings.accounts.removeAccountMessage.defaultMessage: Its folder is deleted for good, with its login on this PC (it doesn't go to the Recycle Bin), and its connections with it. Your conversations and the CLI's memory are kept: they are shared with your other accounts. The account itself stays yours with its provider.
settings.accounts.removeAccountMessage.description: The message of the dialog confirming an account's removal (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107).

settings.accounts.removeConfirm.description: The confirm button of the dialog removing a connection.

settings.accounts.removeFailed.description: An error's title: removing a connection failed.

settings.accounts.removeOpenConfirm.description: The confirm button of that dialog.

settings.accounts.removeOpenTitle.description: Title of the dialog confirming a connection's removal ({name}, its name) while its sign-in or Set Up terminal is open: the terminal is closed first, ending the CLI in it.

settings.accounts.removeTitle.description: Title of the dialog confirming a connection's removal ({name}, its name).

settings.accounts.removing.description: The confirm button of the dialog removing a connection, while it removes it.

settings.accounts.rename.description: Button on a connection (Settings → Accounts & Connections): changes its name only.

settings.accounts.renameConfirm.description: The confirm button of the dialog renaming a connection.

settings.accounts.renameTitle.description: Title of the dialog renaming a connection ({name}, its name).

settings.accounts.sameLoginAccount.defaultMessage: Signed in to the same login as another account: {names}
settings.accounts.sameLoginAccount.description: A warning on an account (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): other accounts are signed in as the same login. {names} is their names, listed.

settings.accounts.setUpChecking.description: A connection's state (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-1870): Hive is still reading whether its coding agent CLI trusts the open workspace's project folders, so it doesn't say yet whether it is set up.

settings.accounts.setUpDone.description: A connection's state (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-1870): its CLI's one-time first-run setup is done. An adjective ("is set up"), not the button.

settings.accounts.setUpIn.defaultMessage: It opens in {project}'s folder, {folder}: answer {cli}'s question to trust it.
settings.accounts.setUpIn.description: Above a connection's Set Up terminal when it opens in a project's folder its coding agent CLI ({cli}) doesn't trust yet (HI-1870): {project} is the project's name, {folder} the folder.

settings.accounts.setUpInWorkspace.defaultMessage: It opens in this workspace's folder, {folder}: answer {cli}'s question to trust it, and every project in it with it.
settings.accounts.setUpInWorkspace.description: Above a connection's Set Up terminal when it opens in the open workspace's folder (HI-1871): the coding agent CLI ({cli}) asks once whether to trust that folder, and trusting it covers every project inside it. {folder} is the folder.

settings.accounts.setUpNeeded.description: A connection's state (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-1870): its CLI's one-time first-run setup (Set Up, a button beside it) hasn't been done in its folder yet.

settings.accounts.signIn.description: Button on a connection (Settings → Accounts & Connections): opens the CLI's own sign-in for it, in a terminal of Hive's.

settings.accounts.signInAgain.description: Button on a connection (Settings → Accounts & Connections) that is signed out, or whose login changed: opens the CLI's own sign-in for it again.

settings.accounts.signInFailed.description: An error's title: a connection's sign-in terminal couldn't be opened.

settings.accounts.signingIn.defaultMessage: Signing in: finish in your browser, or in the terminal below. Combwork doesn't type into it.
settings.accounts.signingIn.description: Settings → Accounts & Connections while a connection's sign-in terminal is open: the user signs in through the CLI's own flow.

settings.accounts.signingInElsewhere.description: A connection's line in Settings → Accounts & Connections while its sign-in is open in another of Hive's windows.

settings.accounts.state.changed.description: A connection's state (Settings → Accounts & Connections): signed in as another login than the one it was added with.

settings.accounts.state.failed.description: A connection's state (Settings → Accounts & Connections): Hive couldn't ask the CLI who it's signed in as (not the same as signed out).

settings.accounts.state.missing.description: A connection's state (Settings → Accounts & Connections): its folder isn't there, or isn't the one Hive made.

settings.accounts.state.signedOut.description: A connection's state (Settings → Accounts & Connections): the CLI says its folder isn't signed in.

settings.accounts.state.unchecked.description: A connection's state (Settings → Accounts & Connections): Hive hasn't asked the CLI yet.

settings.accounts.switchAffected.defaultMessage: Switch Them When Their Turn Is Over
settings.accounts.switchAffected.description: Button on that banner: each of those agents ends once its turn is over and carries on, on the connection chosen now.

settings.accounts.thisPc.description: On GitHub Copilot's account (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): its one sign-in is the PC's, used in every workspace.

settings.accounts.usage.defaultMessage: {window, select, fiveHour {5-hour} weekly {weekly} other {{label}}} {used, number, percent}
settings.accounts.usage.description: An account's plan usage in Settings → Accounts & Connections (HI-2107), once per account: a limit's window (the 5-hour one, the weekly one, or the provider's own name for another) and how much of it is used.

settings.accounts.usageMove.any.description: An entry of the list in an account's usage move ("When it reaches 98% of either limit…", HI-2195): its weekly or its 5-hour limit, whichever gets there first.

settings.accounts.usageMove.failed.description: An error's title: saving an account's usage move failed (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2195).

settings.accounts.usageMove.fiveHour.description: An entry of the list in an account's usage move ("When it reaches 98% of its 5-hour limit…", HI-2195): its plan's rolling 5-hour usage limit.

settings.accounts.usageMove.how.defaultMessage: Each agent moves to the connection with the same name there, or its first one, once its turn is over, and resumes its conversation. The Assistant stays where it is (Settings → Assistant). Combwork moves them once per limit period and never back: move one back by choosing its connection.
settings.accounts.usageMove.how.description: Under an account's usage move when it is on (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2195): what happens.

settings.accounts.usageMove.limitLabel.description: The label, for screen readers, of the list of limits in an account's usage move (HI-2195).

settings.accounts.usageMove.offInAdvance.defaultMessage: Usage moves are turned off in Settings → Advanced: this one does nothing until they are on.
settings.accounts.usageMove.offInAdvance.description: Under an account's usage move (HI-2195) while Settings → Advanced → Move agents at a usage threshold is off. Settings → Advanced names a section.

settings.accounts.usageMove.percentLabel.description: The label, for screen readers, of the number box in an account's usage move (HI-2195): at how many percent of its limit its agents move.

settings.accounts.usageMove.rule.defaultMessage: When it reaches {percent}% of {limit}, move its agents to {target}
settings.accounts.usageMove.rule.description: An account's usage move in Settings → Accounts & Connections (HI-2195), after a checkbox that turns it on. {percent} is a box for a number (98), {limit} a list (its weekly limit, its 5-hour limit, either limit), {target} a list of the CLI's other accounts. Keep all three; their order may change.

settings.accounts.usageMove.targetLabel.description: The label, for screen readers, of the list of accounts in an account's usage move (HI-2195).

settings.accounts.usageMove.turnOn.defaultMessage: Move this account's agents to another account at a usage threshold
settings.accounts.usageMove.turnOn.description: The checkbox's label for screen readers and its tooltip (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2195): turns the account's usage move on or off.

settings.accounts.usageMove.weekly.description: An entry of the list in an account's usage move ("When it reaches 98% of its weekly limit…", HI-2195): its plan's weekly usage limit.

settings.accounts.usedBy.defaultMessage: {assistant, select, yes {{n, plural, =0 {Assistant} one {Assistant and # agent} other {Assistant and # agents}}} other {{n, plural, =0 {Not used here} one {# agent} other {# agents}}}}
settings.accounts.usedBy.description: Who uses a connection, on its row (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): the Assistant (assistant is yes) and how many agents ({n}) of the open workspaces. Its tooltip names them. "Not used here": none in the open workspaces.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.d.defaultMessage: The environment variables Combwork leaves out when it runs Claude Code on a connection (its sign-in, its checks, Set Up and its agents), by name: a key, token, request header, server, provider switch or model set on this PC can't stand in for the connection's own. A server connection's own (its server, key and models) are set after. Wrong, a variable Claude Code reads as a login, a header or a server could make a connection run as someone else, or send a key elsewhere.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.d.description: What the advanced setting "Connections: sign-in variables left out" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.e.defaultMessage: The field of `claude auth status --json` with the email a connection's folder is signed in as. Wrong, Combwork can't tell who a connection is signed in as, and can't warn when its login changes.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.e.description: What the advanced setting "Connections: email field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `claude auth status --json` as it is (a command).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.l.defaultMessage: The field of `claude auth status --json` that says whether a connection's folder is signed in. Wrong, Combwork can't tell, and its sign-in connections show "Couldn't check".
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.l.description: What the advanced setting "Connections: signed-in field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `claude auth status --json` as it is (a command).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.l.defaultMessage: The names of the files in a connection's folder that change when Claude Code signs in or out there, as a regular expression. Combwork watches them (it never reads them) and checks the connection again when one changes. Wrong, a /login or /logout typed in an agent's pane is only found at the connection's next check.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.l.description: What the advanced setting "Connections: login files" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep /login and /logout as they are (commands).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.o.defaultMessage: The field of a connection folder's `.claude.json` that says Claude Code's first-run screens were answered there (read only). Wrong, every Claude Code connection shows "Needs set up" in Settings → Accounts & Connections.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.o.description: What the advanced setting "Connections: set-up field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `.claude.json` as it is (a file name); "Needs set up" is a state Hive shows: use its name as Hive shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.o.defaultMessage: The field of `claude auth status --json` with the organisation's id a connection's folder is signed in to. With the email, it tells two logins apart. Wrong, Combwork can't tell who a connection is signed in as.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.o.description: What the advanced setting "Connections: organisation field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `claude auth status --json` as it is (a command).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.p.defaultMessage: The field of `claude auth status --json` with a connection's plan ("max"), shown beside its email in Settings → Accounts & Connections. Wrong, no plan is shown.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.p.description: What the advanced setting "Connections: plan field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `claude auth status --json` and "max" as they are.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.s.defaultMessage: How long Combwork gives `claude auth status` to say who a connection's folder is signed in as. Past it, the connection shows "Couldn't check", never signed out.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.s.description: What the advanced setting "Connections: sign-in check timeout" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `claude auth status` as it is (a command).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.t.defaultMessage: The field of a folder's entry under `projects` in a connection folder's `.claude.json` that says Claude Code was told to trust that folder (read only). Wrong, every Claude Code connection on in a workspace shows "Needs set up" in Settings → Accounts & Connections.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.t.description: What the advanced setting "Connections: trusted folder field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `projects` and `.claude.json` as they are; "Needs set up" is a state Hive shows: use its name as Hive shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.autoModeSe.defaultMessage: Claude Code offers, now and then in auto mode, to read the project, your recent sessions and optionally your shell history and other repositories, to teach auto mode about your environment. Combwork never answers it: the agent waits for you. Off, Combwork's Claude Code agents are started with the offer turned off for that launch (nothing is written to Claude Code's files, and auto mode decides as before); /auto-mode-setup still runs it when you want.
settings.advanced.claude-code.autoModeSe.description: What the advanced setting "Offer auto mode's environment setup" is for, and what happens when it is off (Settings → Advanced, HI-1959). /auto-mode-setup is Claude Code's command: keep it as it is.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. Auto mode is one of Claude Code's permission modes.

settings.advanced.claude-code.connection.defaultMessage: The model names Ollama runs on ollama.com rather than on this PC (its cloud models, such as gpt-oss:120b-cloud), as a regular expression, for an Ollama connection's models typed in rather than read from Ollama (Read Models asks Ollama, which says). Such a connection's sessions aren't free (local). Wrong, a cloud model typed in is counted as free, or a local one as not free.
settings.advanced.claude-code.connection.description: What the advanced setting "Connections: Ollama cloud models" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Ollama, ollama.com and Read Models (a button) are names; "free (local)" is how Hive shows the cost of sessions run only on this PC.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. Ollama is a product's name; its cloud models run on ollama.com.

settings.advanced.claude-code.exit.comma.defaultMessage: What Combwork types into Claude Code, then Enter, to end it once its lane has ended and its turn is over, so it exits by itself rather than being killed. Wrong, Claude Code isn't ended by it and is killed after the exit grace.
settings.advanced.claude-code.exit.comma.description: What the advanced setting "Lane's end: exit command" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). A lane is a card loop.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.exit.grace.defaultMessage: How long Combwork gives Claude Code to exit by itself after typing its exit command at a lane's end, before killing it. It took {took, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} when recorded.
settings.advanced.claude-code.exit.grace.description: What the advanced setting "Lane's end: exit grace" is for (Settings → Advanced). {took} is how long Claude Code took to exit when recorded, in seconds (1.9).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.know.defaultMessage: The hook events Combwork knows Claude Code sends. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook named outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.know.description: What the advanced setting "Hooks: known events" is for (Settings → Advanced). Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI is another setting's title: use it as Settings shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.know.defaultMessage: The top-level fields Combwork knows Claude Code sends in its hooks. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events: often the first sign that a Claude Code update changed something. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.know.description: What the advanced setting "Hooks: known fields" is for (Settings → Advanced). Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI is another setting's title: use it as Settings shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.preT.defaultMessage: How long Claude Code waits for Combwork's answer before a tool runs (an edit waits for a file lock). If Combwork doesn't answer in time, the tool goes ahead.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.preT.description: What the advanced setting "Hooks: before a tool, timeout" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.time.defaultMessage: How long Claude Code waits for Combwork to take one of its hooks (a turn starting or ending, a notification). Combwork answers at once; raise it only if Combwork's log shows hooks timing out on a slow machine.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.time.description: What the advanced setting "Hooks: timeout" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.memory.rea.defaultMessage: A connection's projects folder is a link to Claude Code's own, so Claude Code asked you before each memory it saved there. Each Claude Code agent on a connection is given its project's auto memory folder by its real path: the same folder, so it saves memories without asking, as it does without a connection. Nothing more is allowed, and nothing is written to Claude Code's files. Off, Claude Code asks before each memory on a connection.
settings.advanced.claude-code.memory.rea.description: What the advanced setting "Auto memory by its real path on connections" is for, and what happens when it is off (Settings → Advanced, HI-1899). settings.advanced.copilot.ready.footer.d.defaultMessage: Copilot only says it has started with the first prompt, so Combwork takes its footer on screen to mean it is ready.
settings.advanced.copilot.ready.footer.d.description: What the advanced setting "Ready footer" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.copilot.ready.footer.t.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.retry.context..defaultMessage: Where Copilot's error hook says a recoverable error happened when it is a model call it tries again (rate-limited, or the service unreachable). Combwork shows the agent's status as waiting to retry until Copilot goes on. Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.copilot.retry.context..description: What the advanced setting "Retry: error context" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. A retry: the coding agent trying its model request again after it failed.

settings.advanced.copilot.retry.message..defaultMessage: How that hook words why the call failed: a regular expression whose named group status is the HTTP status that refused it, whose group limited matches the words of a rate limit (429), or whose group network matches when the service couldn't be reached. Copilot's hook gives the service's own error, often with no status. Wrong, the wait shows without its reason.
settings.advanced.copilot.retry.message..description: What the advanced setting "Retry: error message" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). status, limited and network are the names of the regular expression's groups: keep them.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorMe.defaultMessage: A session error's message, in Copilot's session file, that means its sign-in was refused, when its type doesn't say so.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorMe.description: What the advanced setting "Sign-in refused: error message" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorTy.defaultMessage: A session error's type, in Copilot's session file, that means its sign-in was refused or is missing (#309): Combwork shows the agent signed out.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorTy.description: What the advanced setting "Sign-in refused: error type" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.hookMes.defaultMessage: The message of Copilot's ErrorOccurred hook that means a model call was refused for the sign-in: the turn ends signed out. Another error that ends the turn ends it as failed.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.hookMes.description: What the advanced setting "Sign-in refused: ErrorOccurred hook" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.trust.prompt.d.defaultMessage: Copilot's question before a folder's first session. Combwork shows the agent as waiting for you while it is on screen.
settings.advanced.copilot.trust.prompt.d.description: What the advanced setting "Trust question" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.copilot.trust.prompt.t.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.turnFailed.err.defaultMessage: A session error's type, in Copilot's session file, that means its turn ended because a model call failed after Copilot's retries (it sends no Stop then): Combwork ends the turn as failed, with Copilot's message. Wrong, such an agent shows working until you look.
settings.advanced.copilot.turnFailed.err.description: What the advanced setting "Turn failed: error type" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilotFooter.desc.defaultMessage: Copilot's footer in the {mode} mode ("{footer}"){shared, select, yes {, which Ask and Accept edits share (Combwork tells them apart by the mode the session started in)} other {}}. Combwork reads an agent's mode from its footer (the mode found last on screen), and switches modes by pressing Shift+Tab until the footer shows the one wanted; wrong, Combwork doesn't see the agent in that mode, and can't switch to it without a restart.
settings.advanced.copilotFooter.desc.description: What the advanced setting is for (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot). {mode} is a mode's name; {footer} is Copilot's own footer text, in English: keep it as it is. {shared} is yes for the footer two modes share.

settings.advanced.copilotFooter.title.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot): the footer Copilot shows in a mode. {mode} is the mode's name.

settings.advanced.data.desc.description: What the setting "Settings file" does, under its title (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.data.tip.defaultMessage: Project settings live in each project's .hive folder; workspace settings in the workspace .hive folder.
settings.advanced.data.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Settings file" (Settings → Advanced): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.advanced.error.badPattern.description: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {why} the browser engine's own reason, in English.

settings.advanced.error.boolean.description: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; true and false are the values as written: keep them.

settings.advanced.error.choice.description: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {choices} lists the values it takes as advanced.json writes them (allow, ask, block): keep them.

settings.advanced.error.field.defaultMessage: {title} takes a field name: letters, digits and _ (not starting with a digit).
settings.advanced.error.field.description: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken: it must be a field name of a CLI's data. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.folders.defaultMessage: {title} takes up to {most} folders, each a full path (C:\…, \\server\…, or starting with a variable such as %LOCALAPPDATA%), separated by semicolons.
settings.advanced.error.folders.description: Why an advanced setting's new value (a list of folders) isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {most} a number of folders. C:\…, \\server\… and %LOCALAPPDATA% are written as Windows writes them: keep them.

settings.advanced.error.list.defaultMessage: {title} takes 1 to 10 names (letters, digits, - and _), as a list or separated by commas.
settings.advanced.error.list.description: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.matchesAll.defaultMessage: {title} would match anything (it matches empty text).
settings.advanced.error.matchesAll.description: Why an advanced setting's new value (a regular expression) isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.number.defaultMessage: {title} takes a whole number from {min} to {max}.
settings.advanced.error.number.description: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {min} and {max} are numbers.

settings.advanced.error.oneLine.defaultMessage: {title} takes one line of at most {most} characters.
settings.advanced.error.oneLine.description: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {most} a number of characters.

settings.advanced.error.pattern.description: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken (Settings → Advanced). {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.text.description: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.hive.accounts.usageMov.defaultMessage: Move an account's agents to another account when it reaches the share of its limit set on it in Settings → Accounts & Connections. Turned off, no account moves its agents and moves waiting for an agent's turn to end are dropped; the rules are kept.
settings.advanced.hive.accounts.usageMov.description: What the advanced setting "Move agents at a usage threshold" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Settings → Accounts & Connections names a section.

settings.advanced.hive.accounts.usageMov.defaultMessage: Move agents at a usage threshold
settings.advanced.hive.accounts.usageMov.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. An account in Settings → Accounts & Connections can move its agents to another account when it has used a share of its plan's limit.

settings.advanced.hive.assistant.startVi.defaultMessage: While the Assistant's journal is on, Combwork gives it a short view of the workspace when it starts and after each compaction: what is under way and waiting, and the journal's recent entries. Turned off, it gets none from its next start or compaction on, a running Assistant too, and reads what it needs with its tools.
settings.advanced.hive.assistant.startVi.description: What the advanced setting "The Assistant starts with Hive's start view" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive).

settings.advanced.hive.assistant.startVi.defaultMessage: The Assistant starts with Combwork's start view
settings.advanced.hive.assistant.startVi.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. The start view is what Hive tells the Hive Assistant of the workspace's state as it starts.

settings.advanced.hive.cards.attachmentF.defaultMessage: More folders an agent, the Assistant or a script may attach files to a card from, besides its own project's folders and the temp folder: full paths, separated by semicolons (%LOCALAPPDATA% and other variables at the start are filled in). Another project's folders and Combwork's own stay refused, even inside one. Empty: none.
settings.advanced.hive.cards.attachmentF.description: What the advanced setting "Card attachments: more folders" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). %LOCALAPPDATA% is a Windows variable: keep it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by a list of folders: where else agents may attach files to a card from.

settings.advanced.hive.cards.attachmentM.defaultMessage: The largest file Combwork keeps with a card, in bytes: pasted or dropped into the card, attached from an agent's pane, or given by an agent or the Assistant. A larger file is refused, saying so. Files already kept stay.
settings.advanced.hive.cards.attachmentM.description: What the advanced setting "Card attachments: largest file" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in bytes: the largest file Hive keeps with a card (pasted, dropped or attached to it).

settings.advanced.hive.cards.titleNudgeC.defaultMessage: When an agent or the Assistant gives a card a title longer than this, Combwork keeps it and tells the agent a shorter one would be better: a long title is cut in git's history, where it becomes the merge commit's subject, and on the board. The titles you write yourself are never questioned. 0 turns the suggestion off.
settings.advanced.hive.cards.titleNudgeC.description: What the advanced setting "Suggest a shorter title past" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A card title is the one-line name of a card on the task board.

An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in characters ("80 characters"): the length of a card title an agent writes past which Hive suggests a shorter one.

settings.advanced.hive.console.showText..defaultMessage: Show the text in the developer console: prompts, replies, commands and tools' arguments, under a banner saying it is unredacted, and start each recording with its text box ticked. Tokens, API keys and sign-in details stay masked whatever this says; agents' cw_console stays redacted, and a recording with text is never attached to Copy Diagnostics.
settings.advanced.hive.console.showText..description: What the advanced setting "Developer console: show prompt, reply and command text" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.console.showText..defaultMessage: Developer console: show prompt, reply and command text
settings.advanced.hive.console.showText..description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.copies.quietWaitM.defaultMessage: A returned review or check copy is used again only once nothing is running in it: no run, no process its check started, its reviewer idle. Past this many minutes, a check waiting for a copy says which copy is still in use and by what. Combwork never resets a copy something is still running in.
settings.advanced.hive.copies.quietWaitM.description: What the advanced setting "Copies: wait for one to be free" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive).

settings.advanced.hive.copies.quietWaitM.defaultMessage: Copies: wait for one to be free
settings.advanced.hive.copies.quietWaitM.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in minutes ("10 min"). A copy is a folder Hive keeps at one revision for a review or an isolated check.

settings.advanced.hive.copies.review.des.defaultMessage: A reviewer reads a card's work, and runs its commands, in a review copy: a folder at exactly the revision under review, which nothing else writes, so what it checks is what was submitted. Turned off, reviewers read the builder's folder as before. Isolated checks (hive-progress --check with --isolated) use the same copies either way.
settings.advanced.hive.copies.review.des.description: What the advanced setting "Reviewers review in review copies" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). hive-progress --check and --isolated are a command and its options: keep them as they are.

settings.advanced.hive.copies.review.tit.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. A review copy is a folder Hive keeps at the exact revision a reviewer reviews, which nothing else writes.

settings.advanced.hive.disableHardwareAc.defaultMessage: Draw Combwork without the graphics card, for a graphics driver that leaves Combwork's window blank, flickering or crashing. Terminals then draw without WebGL. Takes effect when Combwork restarts; to start once without it, run Combwork with --disable-gpu.
settings.advanced.hive.disableHardwareAc.description: What the advanced setting "Disable hardware acceleration" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). --disable-gpu is a command-line option: keep it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.focused.pickSecon.defaultMessage: How long the project’s command that chooses a card’s focused tests may run, when it is submitted and at its merge. Past it, the command is ended and no tests count as chosen: the builder then names them itself.
settings.advanced.hive.focused.pickSecon.description: What the advanced setting "Focused tests: longest the choice of tests runs" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.focused.pickSecon.defaultMessage: Focused tests: longest the choice of tests runs
settings.advanced.hive.focused.pickSecon.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in seconds: how long the project's command that chooses a card's focused tests may run, when the card is submitted and at its merge.

settings.advanced.hive.guidance.desc.defaultMessage: With Combwork's tools, each project agent gets Combwork's guidance: how to use the tools, the board and handovers, and its project's latest handover. Claude Code and Copilot get it as the hive server's instructions, Codex after your own developer_instructions. Turned off, agents still get Combwork's tools, without the guidance, from their next session. The Assistant always gets its own: they are its role.
settings.advanced.hive.guidance.desc.description: What the advanced setting "Hive's guidance for agents" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Claude Code, Copilot and Codex are CLIs' names, hive the name of Hive's MCP server and developer_instructions a Codex setting: keep them.

settings.advanced.hive.guidance.title.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: the instructions Hive gives project agents on how to work with it.

settings.advanced.hive.heapSnapshotNearL.defaultMessage: When Combwork's main process nears its memory limit, it writes a snapshot of its memory to the heap folder in Combwork's profile before it closes, to find out what filled it. A snapshot can be several gigabytes, holds whatever Combwork had in memory (card text, transcripts, possibly tokens) and stays on this PC; Combwork keeps the newest two. Takes effect when Combwork restarts.
settings.advanced.hive.heapSnapshotNearL.description: What the advanced setting "Save a memory snapshot if Hive is about to run out of memory" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.heapSnapshotNearL.defaultMessage: Save a memory snapshot if Combwork is about to run out of memory
settings.advanced.hive.heapSnapshotNearL.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.hooks.missingSeco.defaultMessage: How long an agent's CLI may go without a hook, from its start (a CLI that sends one then) or from a prompt it went to work on, before Combwork says its hooks aren't arriving and shows its status as unknown (#1336). A long think after a prompt's hook never counts. Raise it if a slow machine shows that notice for agents that are fine.
settings.advanced.hive.hooks.missingSeco.description: What the advanced setting "Hooks missing: wait" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. Hooks: the calls an agent's coding agent makes to Hive as it works.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.checkpoints.defaultMessage: When something arrives in a working agent's inbox, Combwork tells it at the end of its next tool call, in that tool's reply, so it can read it without stopping. Turned off, a working agent isn't told until its turn ends or it is idle; nothing is lost, as it stays in the inbox. A project can set its own in Project Settings → Sessions.
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.checkpoints.description: What the advanced setting "Tell a working agent at the end of a tool" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Project Settings → Sessions names a section of the project's settings: use its name as Hive shows it.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.checkpoints.defaultMessage: Tell a working agent at the end of a tool
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.checkpoints.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: Hive tells a busy agent what has arrived in its inbox each time one of its tool calls ends.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.idleWakes.d.defaultMessage: When something arrives in an idle agent's inbox, Combwork types one short line into its terminal saying so, which wakes it. Card loops' wakes (the workflow option Wake reviewers and builders) and card watches' are such wakes. Turned off, nothing is typed for anything waiting: it stays in the inbox, the agent's pane shows how many, and its Deliver Now types the line once. A card started on an agent, or a task given to it now, is still typed. A project can set its own in Project Settings → Sessions.
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.idleWakes.d.description: What the advanced setting "Wake an idle agent" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Wake reviewers and builders names a workflow option and Project Settings → Sessions a section, Deliver Now a menu item: use their names as Hive shows them.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.idleWakes.t.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: Hive types a short line into an idle agent's terminal to tell it something has arrived in its inbox.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.stopContinu.defaultMessage: When an agent is about to end its turn with items in its inbox it hasn't read, Combwork keeps it going to read them first, once a turn: Codex and Copilot by holding their stop back, Claude Code by adding a line to its stop. Turned off, the turn ends as the CLI ends it, and the items wait in the inbox for an idle wake. A project can set its own in Project Settings → Sessions.
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.stopContinu.description: What the advanced setting "Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Codex, Copilot and Claude Code are CLIs' names: keep them. Project Settings → Sessions names a section of the project's settings: use its name as Hive shows it.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.stopContinu.defaultMessage: Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.stopContinu.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: when an agent is about to end its turn with items in its inbox it hasn't read, Hive makes it carry on and read them.

settings.advanced.hive.journal.builds.de.defaultMessage: When Combwork's own installer is built from its source code (npm run dist, or npm run release), Combwork writes the build into the Assistant's journal as its own entry: the version, the commit, what kind of build it was and where the installer is. Only a successful build is written, and only while the journal is on with events in its scope. Turned off, builds aren't written, and a build left for Combwork while it was closed is dropped when the workspace opens.
settings.advanced.hive.journal.builds.de.description: What the advanced setting "Record builds in the journal" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). npm run dist and npm run release are commands: keep them as they are.

settings.advanced.hive.journal.builds.ti.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. The journal is the Hive Assistant's record of decisions and events; builds are installers made from Hive's own source code.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.endWaitMinu.defaultMessage: How long, from a lane's end, Combwork waits for its builder to finish its turn and read that the lane is finished. Past it, Combwork ends the builder's CLI anyway: with its exit command, or killed when that can't be typed (your draft is in its prompt) or doesn't end it.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.endWaitMinu.description: What the advanced setting "Lanes: longest a lane's end waits for its builder" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A lane is a card loop.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.endWaitMinu.defaultMessage: Lanes: longest a lane's end waits for its builder
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.endWaitMinu.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in minutes ("10 min"). A lane is a card loop: a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.freshStartW.defaultMessage: A lane starts its agents in new conversations. One that is busy as the lane starts (in a turn, or reading a message Combwork just gave it) is started once it is free, for up to this long. After that Combwork stops trying: the lane's row says so, and you retry it there or end the lane. Combwork never interrupts a turn for it, and never gives the lane's cards to the old conversation.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.freshStartW.description: What the advanced setting "Lanes: longest Hive waits to start a busy agent afresh" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A lane is a card loop.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.freshStartW.defaultMessage: Lanes: longest Combwork waits to start a busy agent afresh
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.freshStartW.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in minutes ("10 min"). A lane is a card loop: a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.gentleEnd.d.defaultMessage: When a lane's last card merges (or the lane is abandoned), Combwork waits for its builder's turn to end, tells it the lane is finished with each card's merge commit, then ends its CLI with the CLI's own exit command, killing it only if it doesn't exit. Its slot stays its until then. Turned off, Combwork stops the builder's session as soon as it is first idle, as before.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.gentleEnd.d.description: What the advanced setting "Lanes: let the builder finish when its lane ends" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A lane is a card loop; a slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.gentleEnd.t.defaultMessage: Lanes: let the builder finish when its lane ends
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.gentleEnd.t.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. A lane is a card loop: a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.unwatchedNo.defaultMessage: When the Assistant may control agents (Settings → Assistant → Control) and is about to end its turn while lanes are running and no watch of its covers them, Combwork keeps it going once to say so, naming the lanes' builders, so it watches them before it finishes. At Look and advise the lanes are yours to run, and it isn't told. Turned off, its turn ends as its CLI ends it, and nothing wakes it about those lanes until it watches them again.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.unwatchedNo.description: What the advanced setting "Lanes: remind the Assistant to watch them" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A lane is a card loop; a watch is what wakes an agent when the cards or lanes it follows change.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.unwatchedNo.defaultMessage: Lanes: remind the Assistant to watch them
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.unwatchedNo.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. A lane is a card loop: a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn; the Assistant is the Hive Assistant.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitReviewe.defaultMessage: After how long a lane whose card waits in Review with nobody reviewing it has its wait marked in the Progress panel's Lanes. Too short marks every review; too long, a card can sit unreviewed.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitReviewe.description: What the advanced setting "Lanes: a long wait for a reviewer" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitReviewe.defaultMessage: Lanes: a long wait for a reviewer
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitReviewe.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitYouMinu.defaultMessage: After how long a lane waiting for you (a request in For you, or a card at its round limit) has its wait marked in the Progress panel's Lanes. Too short marks every wait; too long, a lane can sit unnoticed.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitYouMinu.description: What the advanced setting "Lanes: a long wait for you" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitYouMinu.defaultMessage: Lanes: a long wait for you
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitYouMinu.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.lostLine.steadySe.defaultMessage: A line Combwork typed into an agent that its CLI didn't take, gone from its input since (a screen of the CLI's took it): how long its input must stay empty, at its prompt, with nothing taken, before Combwork types it again or, with nothing to type again, tells you. Raise it if a slow machine has a line typed twice.
settings.advanced.hive.lostLine.steadySe.description: What the advanced setting "Lost line: wait" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced, HI-1959).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. A line: a message Hive typed into an agent's terminal.

settings.advanced.hive.mcp.connectSecond.defaultMessage: How long Combwork waits, once an agent is ready, for its CLI to connect Combwork's tools before it tells the agent of new work anyway. A resumed session can be ready before its tools are, and a message then is a turn spent without them (#865). Lower it if messages reach agents late when their CLI doesn't connect Combwork's tools.
settings.advanced.hive.mcp.connectSecond.description: What the advanced setting "hive tools: wait to connect" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.mcp.replySeconds..defaultMessage: How long the hive MCP server waits for Combwork to answer one of its tools (a wait's own time comes on top). Raise it when a slow or very busy machine makes hive tools fail with "Combwork didn't reply within 300 s" (#371).
settings.advanced.hive.mcp.replySeconds..description: What the advanced setting "hive tools: reply timeout" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.downlo.defaultMessage: How long Install and Update wait for a catalogue server's zip, redirects included, before they stop with nothing installed. Raise it on a slow connection.
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.downlo.description: What the advanced setting "MCP catalogues: downloading a server" is for (Settings → Advanced, HI-545).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds (HI-545).

settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.fetchS.defaultMessage: How long the MCP view waits for a catalogue's list, redirects included, before it shows that catalogue couldn't be read. Raise it on a slow connection.
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.fetchS.description: What the advanced setting "MCP catalogues: reading one" is for (Settings → Advanced, HI-545).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds. An MCP catalogue is a list of servers to install (HI-545).

settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.probeS.defaultMessage: How long each check of this PC for a catalogue server's requirements (its Windows edition and build, Node.js, Docker) may take before it shows as not checked.
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.probeS.description: What the advanced setting "MCP catalogues: checking this PC’s requirements" is for (Settings → Advanced, HI-545).

settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.probeS.defaultMessage: MCP catalogues: checking this PC's requirements
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.probeS.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds (HI-545).

settings.advanced.hive.merge.lockWaitSec.defaultMessage: How long a merge, or another change to a repository's branches (a pull, switching branch, moving an agent's branch), waits while another Combwork on this computer is merging into the same repository. After it, nothing is changed and Combwork says which Combwork holds the repository: try again once it has finished. Combwork never takes the repository from a Combwork that is still running.
settings.advanced.hive.merge.lockWaitSec.description: What the advanced setting "Merges: wait for another Hive" is for, and what happens when the wait ends (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. Another Hive: the installed Hive and a dev or test Hive on the same machine.

settings.advanced.hive.none.baselineSeco.defaultMessage: In a project without version control, Combwork reads the project's files in the background when a card starts, when it is submitted, and when a check of it starts and ends, to find what changed outside the card's files. A read that takes longer than this is stopped: the card starts or is submitted without that list, and the check doesn't count.
settings.advanced.hive.none.baselineSeco.description: What the advanced setting "No version control: longest read of the project" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive).

settings.advanced.hive.none.baselineSeco.defaultMessage: No version control: longest read of the project
settings.advanced.hive.none.baselineSeco.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in seconds ("120 s"). In a project without version control, Hive reads every file of the project in the background when a card starts.

settings.advanced.hive.notes.deliverWork.defaultMessage: Each agent and the Assistant get the shared note Workspace notes in their instructions when they start, on every CLI and in whichever folder they work: notes about this machine that no committed file should hold. A project's agents get the parts for everyone and their own project's section. Turned off, or with the note empty, nothing is added, from each agent's next session.
settings.advanced.hive.notes.deliverWork.description: What the advanced setting "Deliver workspace notes to agents" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Workspace notes is the name of a shared note: keep it in English, as the Notes view shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: Hive gives every agent the shared note Workspace notes when it starts.

settings.advanced.hive.notes.workspaceNo.defaultMessage: How much of the shared note Workspace notes an agent's instructions get, at most, in bytes. A longer note is cut, and agents are told to read the note for the rest. Every agent reads it at every start, so a short note costs less.
settings.advanced.hive.notes.workspaceNo.description: What the advanced setting "Workspace notes: most an agent gets" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Workspace notes is the name of a shared note: keep it in English, as the Notes view shows it.

settings.advanced.hive.notes.workspaceNo.defaultMessage: Workspace notes: most an agent gets
settings.advanced.hive.notes.workspaceNo.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in bytes: how much of the shared note Workspace notes an agent's instructions get at most.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkFirst.defaultMessage: How long after the turn ends Combwork first checks the connection. Each check that finds it still down doubles the wait before the next, up to the longest wait below.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkFirst.description: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: first check after" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkFirst.defaultMessage: Resuming after a connection drops: first check after
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkFirst.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("30 s").

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkMostS.defaultMessage: The longest Combwork waits between two checks of the connection.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkMostS.description: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: longest wait between checks" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkMostS.defaultMessage: Resuming after a connection drops: longest wait between checks
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkMostS.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("300 s").

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.defaultMessage: The address Combwork asks to see whether Claude Code's connection is back: its API host. Any reply counts, an error page too. An agent on a server connection is checked at its server's address instead.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.description: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for Claude Code" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.defaultMessage: Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for Claude Code
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. Claude Code is a product name.
