settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.description: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for Codex" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.defaultMessage: Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for Codex
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. Codex is a product name.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.defaultMessage: The address Combwork asks to see whether GitHub Copilot's connection is back: its API host. Any reply counts, an error page too.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.description: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for GitHub Copilot" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.defaultMessage: Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for GitHub Copilot
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. GitHub Copilot is a product name.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.notConnect.defaultMessage: A failed turn whose error this regular expression finds is never resumed, whatever a CLI's connection error pattern finds: a usage or rate limit, a sign-in, an overloaded server. Resuming wouldn't help those, and could repeat.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.notConnect.description: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: errors that are never a dropped connection" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.notConnect.defaultMessage: Resuming after a connection drops: errors that are never a dropped connection
settings.advanced.hive.outage.notConnect.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.resume.des.defaultMessage: When an agent's turn ends because its CLI couldn't reach its API (a router restarting, Wi-Fi dropping), Combwork shows it waiting for the connection, checks the CLI's API host now and then, and once it answers tells the agent to rerun what was cut off and carry on. Never for a usage limit, an expired sign-in or an overloaded server. After three resumes in an hour that end the same way, or once the wait's limit passes, Combwork stops and says what to try.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resume.des.description: What the advanced setting "Resume agents after a connection drops" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.resume.tit.defaultMessage: Resume agents after a connection drops
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resume.tit.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.resumesPer.defaultMessage: How many times in an hour Combwork resumes the same agent. Once its turn ends on a connection error again after that many, Combwork stops: the PC's own network may not have recovered.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resumesPer.description: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: resumes in an hour" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.resumesPer.defaultMessage: Resuming after a connection drops: resumes in an hour
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resumesPer.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by a number.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.waitMinute.defaultMessage: How long Combwork waits for the connection to come back before it stops waiting and tells you.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.waitMinute.description: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: wait at most" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.waitMinute.defaultMessage: Resuming after a connection drops: wait at most
settings.advanced.hive.outage.waitMinute.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in minutes ("120 min").

settings.advanced.hive.processes.orphanN.defaultMessage: When a process an agent's command started is still running ten minutes on with the shell that started it gone, Combwork says so once in a notice, and tells the agent once at its next tool call or turn's end, so it can end it. Turned off, neither is told; Activity still lists the process as left running, with End It.
settings.advanced.hive.processes.orphanN.description: What the advanced setting "Processes left running: tell me and the agent" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Activity is a tab of Hive's; End It is its button.

settings.advanced.hive.processes.orphanN.defaultMessage: Processes left running: tell me and the agent
settings.advanced.hive.processes.orphanN.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: a process an agent's command left running, its shell gone, is told in a notice and to the agent.

settings.advanced.hive.progress.lanesSho.defaultMessage: How many card-loop lanes the Progress panel shows before its lanes scroll, until you drag the section's top edge (the drag is kept per workspace). A workspace that runs many lanes at once can set its own.
settings.advanced.hive.progress.lanesSho.description: What the advanced setting "Progress panel: lanes shown" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.progress.replySec.defaultMessage: How long hive-progress waits for Combwork to answer before a command or a check starts, and for its start to be taken. A check needs the answer (its command is the project's): with none, it asks once more, then runs nothing and says Combwork is slow. Raise it when a busy Combwork makes checks fail with "Combwork is slow to answer" (HI-1892). Kept at 2 minutes at most.
settings.advanced.hive.progress.replySec.description: What the advanced setting "hive-progress: Hive's reply time" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. hive-progress is the command agents run long commands and checks through: keep it as it is.

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.asTyped.de.defaultMessage: Combwork puts each prompt it types into an agent (a message, a wake, a card's start) on one line: runs of spaces become one, line breaks become spaces, and control characters are left out. Turned on, Claude Code and Copilot get the text as written, spacing and line breaks included. Codex, and a slash command in any CLI, still get each line break and tab as a space: Combwork types those key by key, where a line break would send the prompt early and a tab complete a word. For Codex, Typed prompts: line breaks (under Codex) can press a new-line key instead. Other control characters are left out either way: they would press keys.
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.asTyped.de.description: What the advanced setting "Send prompts as typed" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Claude Code, Copilot and Codex are CLIs' names: keep them.

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.asTyped.ti.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: the prompts Hive itself types into agents' CLIs.

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.clearDraft.defaultMessage: Before Combwork types a prompt or Compact into an agent's CLI, it presses Ctrl+U, which clears what is in the CLI's input, and it presses it again to take back a prompt it stopped part-way. Turned off, Combwork never presses it: text left in the CLI's input stays in front of what Combwork types and is sent with it, a prompt stopped part-way stays in the input, and Compact can fail behind a draft. Changing Codex's mode still clears its input first, as its menu needs.
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.clearDraft.description: What the advanced setting "Clear the CLI's draft before Hive types" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Ctrl+U names keys: use the key names your language uses. Compact is a command's name: use it as Hive shows it.

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.clearDraft.defaultMessage: Clear the CLI's draft before Combwork types
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.clearDraft.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. The draft is text left in the input of an agent's CLI, not sent yet.

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.rawCardSta.defaultMessage: When a card is started on an agent, Combwork gives it the card wrapped in its own words: which card it is on the board, what it depends on and which docs to read first, and which skill to follow. Turned on, the agent gets only the card's title and description, and what you wrote when you started it. Combwork's other prompts (its wakes and messages) stay as they are: they are how Combwork and its agents talk.
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.rawCardSta.description: What the advanced setting "A card's start in its own words" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive).

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.rawCardSta.defaultMessage: A card's start in its own words
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.rawCardSta.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: what Hive types into an agent when a card is started on it.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkMinute.defaultMessage: How long the merge queue lets one merge check or install run before it ends it. A check ended this way is a failure of the environment, not of the work: the card comes back marked so, and its builder can send the same revision back into the queue. Raise it when a project’s checks really take longer; too long, and a hung check holds the queue up that long.
settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkMinute.description: What the advanced setting "Merge queue: longest a merge check runs" does, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkMinute.defaultMessage: Merge queue: longest a merge check runs
settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkMinute.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in minutes ("90 min"). A merge check is a command (tests, a build) Hive runs on a card's merged result before it moves the target.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT.description: A choice of the advanced setting "Merge queue: merge into a checked-out branch": ask the user (For you) before each update of the folder.
A choice of the advanced setting "Merge queue: merge into a checked-out branch": update the folder without asking.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT.defaultMessage: When the branch the merge queue merges into is checked out in a folder (the project folder's main, say), merging changes that folder's files too. Ask each time waits, once a card is tested and ready, for you to approve updating the folder in For you. Automatically updates it at once. Either way the queue first checks that no agent is working in the folder, that it is on that branch and that you have no changes in the files the merge changes, and pauses if not. One rare race, another program switching that folder's branch in the same instant, can leave the merged files in the other branch; Combwork then says so and lists them. A branch checked out nowhere is always merged at once.
settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT.description: What the advanced setting "Merge queue: merge into a checked-out branch" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Ask each time and Automatically are the setting's choices: use the words its list shows. For you is a place in Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT.defaultMessage: Merge queue: merge into a checked-out branch
settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: what the merge queue does when the branch it merges into (main, say) is checked out in a folder, usually the project folder, whose files then change.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.focusedJobs.defaultMessage: How many tests at once the merge queue’s run of a card’s focused tests may use, passed to the project’s command that runs them. More finishes sooner but loads the computer, which agents and your own work share.
settings.advanced.hive.queue.focusedJobs.description: What the advanced setting "Merge queue: focused tests run at once" does, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.queue.focusedJobs.defaultMessage: Merge queue: focused tests run at once
settings.advanced.hive.queue.focusedJobs.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by a number: how many of a card's focused tests (the tests its change needs) the merge queue runs in parallel.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.networkCode.defaultMessage: A failed merge check whose last 40 lines of output this regular expression finds failed for the network, not the work: the card is returned to its builder marked temporary, and the builder may submit the same revision again (at most twice in a row) instead of a new one. The default finds Node's and npm's network error codes (ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT). A project's check can also say so itself by exiting with code 75. (?!) finds nothing: then only a check that couldn't start, ran out of time or was ended counts as temporary.
settings.advanced.hive.queue.networkCode.description: What the advanced setting "Merge queue: network errors that count as temporary" does (Settings → Advanced). The error codes, (?!) and 75 are literal: keep them.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.networkCode.defaultMessage: Merge queue: network errors that count as temporary
settings.advanced.hive.queue.networkCode.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. The merge queue tests a card's work before merging it; a check that fails for the network, not the work, lets the card's builder submit the same revision again.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.signSeconds.defaultMessage: When a repository signs its commits, how long the merge queue waits for its merge commit, hooks included, before it takes the signer to be waiting for a passphrase. It then ends the commit, changes nothing in the target and pauses the queue with “signing waits for you”. Raise it when signing or the repository’s commit hooks really take longer; too long, and a signer waiting for you holds the queue up that long.
settings.advanced.hive.queue.signSeconds.description: What the advanced setting "Merge queue: longest a signed merge commit takes" does, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). “signing waits for you” is how the queue’s pause reads.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.signSeconds.defaultMessage: Merge queue: longest a signed merge commit takes
settings.advanced.hive.queue.signSeconds.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in seconds ("60 s"). The merge commit is the commit Hive's merge queue makes when it merges a card; signed means the repository is set to sign commits (GPG or SSH).

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.afterSec.defaultMessage: How long a capture waits after its trigger before it is saved, so it holds what followed too: what the CLI did next.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.afterSec.description: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: wait after a trigger" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.afterSec.defaultMessage: Flight recorder: wait after a trigger
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.afterSec.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("10 s").

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.keep.des.defaultMessage: How many captures Combwork keeps in its console-recordings folder: past it, the oldest go. Recordings you made in the developer console are never removed.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.keep.des.description: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: captures kept" does (Settings → Advanced). console-recordings is a folder name: keep it.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.minutes..defaultMessage: How long after a capture the same trigger waits before it captures the same agent again, so something that keeps happening saves one capture, not many.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.minutes..description: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: one capture per trigger and agent every" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.minutes..defaultMessage: Flight recorder: one capture per trigger and agent every
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.minutes..description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in minutes ("10 min").

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.pattern..defaultMessage: Save a capture when an agent's developer console event has a name or summary this regular expression finds (case-insensitive). The default, (?!), never finds anything: it is off.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.pattern..description: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: capture events matching" does (Settings → Advanced). (?!) is a regular expression: keep it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. The flight recorder saves the developer console's recent events when something rare happens.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.safeguar.defaultMessage: Save a capture when a model's safeguards stop a response or switch the model: the agent's newest developer console events, redacted, in Combwork's console-recordings folder, with a notice. With any flight recorder trigger on, Combwork keeps each agent's newest developer console events in memory (redacted), whether a console is open or not.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.safeguar.description: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: capture safeguard stops" does (Settings → Advanced). console-recordings is a folder name: keep it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. The flight recorder saves the developer console's recent events when something rare happens.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.stalled..defaultMessage: Save a capture when an agent working on a turn goes silent past its limit, so Combwork can't tell what it is doing.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.stalled..description: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: capture an agent gone silent" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.stalled..defaultMessage: Flight recorder: capture an agent gone silent
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.stalled..description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. The flight recorder saves the developer console's recent events when something rare happens.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.unknown..defaultMessage: Save a capture when a CLI sends a hook or a status line with a field Combwork doesn't know: often the first sign that a CLI update changed something.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.unknown..description: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI" does (Settings → Advanced). A hook and a status line are what a CLI sends Hive as it works.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.unknown..defaultMessage: Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.unknown..description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. The flight recorder saves the developer console's recent events when something rare happens.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.version..defaultMessage: Save a capture when an agent starts on a version of its CLI other than the one the last agent of that CLI started on.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.version..description: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: capture a CLI version change" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.version..defaultMessage: Flight recorder: capture a CLI version change
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.version..description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. The flight recorder saves the developer console's recent events when something rare happens.

settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeAft.defaultMessage: When Combwork restarts for an update (Restart to Update, or an installer closing it), the agents that were working, watching their cards or in a card loop start again in their conversations, one at a time, each told where it was. Off: Combwork offers to resume them instead, as it does after you quit.
settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeAft.description: What the advanced setting "Resume agents after an update" does (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeRea.defaultMessage: How long an agent Combwork resumes after a restart has to be ready. One that isn't is stopped and listed as not resumed, and the next one starts.
settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeRea.description: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a restart: ready within" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeRea.defaultMessage: Resuming after a restart: ready within
settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeRea.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("90 s").

settings.advanced.hive.retry.tellAssista.defaultMessage: How long an agent's coding agent may keep waiting to retry its model request (rate-limited, or its service unreachable) in one turn before Combwork tells the Assistant, once a turn. 0: never.
settings.advanced.hive.retry.tellAssista.description: What the advanced setting "Retry wait: tell the Assistant after" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.retry.tellAssista.defaultMessage: Retry wait: tell the Assistant after
settings.advanced.hive.retry.tellAssista.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("300 s"). A retry wait: an agent's coding agent waiting to try its model request again.

settings.advanced.hive.sessions.terminal.defaultMessage: Combwork starts each session with TERM=xterm-256color, as its terminal is, and without Windows Terminal's WT_SESSION, so the CLIs draw the same whether Combwork was opened from the Start menu or a terminal (Claude Code draws ❯ rather than >). A TERM in your own environment or the session's is kept. Turned off, sessions get the environment Combwork was opened with.
settings.advanced.hive.sessions.terminal.description: What the advanced setting "Sessions say their terminal is xterm-256color" does (Settings → Advanced). TERM, WT_SESSION and xterm-256color are names: keep them; ❯ and > are the characters Claude Code draws as its prompt mark.

settings.advanced.hive.sessions.terminal.defaultMessage: Sessions say their terminal is xterm-256color
settings.advanced.hive.sessions.terminal.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. xterm-256color is a terminal type's name and TERM an environment variable's: keep them.

settings.advanced.hive.showDeveloperFeat.defaultMessage: Show Help → Developer Console (Ctrl+Alt+J): what each CLI sends Combwork, next to what Combwork made of it.
settings.advanced.hive.showDeveloperFeat.description: What the advanced setting "Show developer features" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.skills.removeIdle.defaultMessage: Codex and Copilot read Combwork's skills from copies Combwork puts in each agent's folder (.agents/skills/hive-…); Claude Code gets them at each launch and leaves nothing behind. Once the last of Combwork's agents in a folder stops, Combwork can remove its copies, so a CLI you run there yourself doesn't see them. Slots only removes them from slots and agents' worktrees, never the project folder. Everywhere removes them from the project folder too. Never keeps them. Only copies Combwork made, and nobody changed since, are removed: never your own skills.
settings.advanced.hive.skills.removeIdle.description: What the advanced setting "Remove Hive's skill copies when no agent works in the folder" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Codex, Copilot and Claude Code are CLIs' names and .agents/skills/hive-… a folder: keep them. Slots only, Everywhere and Never are the setting's choices: use the words its list shows.
A choice of the advanced setting "Remove Hive's skill copies when no agent works in the folder": in the project folder too.
A choice of the advanced setting "Remove Hive's skill copies when no agent works in the folder": copies stay, as before.
A choice of the advanced setting "Remove Hive's skill copies when no agent works in the folder": in every folder but the project folder.

settings.advanced.hive.skills.removeIdle.defaultMessage: Remove Combwork's skill copies when no agent works in the folder
settings.advanced.hive.skills.removeIdle.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: the copies of Hive's skills it puts in a folder for Codex and Copilot.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.deleteMerge.defaultMessage: Each card built in a slot works on a branch of its own, such as hive/AM/AM-12-fix-the-login. Once the card is Done and its target branch contains the branch's work (a squash merge too), Combwork deletes the branch and notes it on the card. A branch with work that isn't merged, or checked out somewhere, is never deleted. Turned off, the branches stay.
settings.advanced.hive.slots.deleteMerge.description: What the advanced setting "Delete a card's branch once it's merged" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane. Keep hive/AM/AM-12-fix-the-login as it is (an example branch name).

settings.advanced.hive.slots.deleteMerge.defaultMessage: Delete a card's branch once it's merged
settings.advanced.hive.slots.deleteMerge.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. Each card built in a slot (a worktree Hive lends) gets a branch of its own.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.removeIdle..defaultMessage: A project keeps as many slots as it has builders. A free slot beyond that, unused for a day, is removed: its archive command runs first, and it is kept if that fails. Combwork never removes one with an agent or a process in it, a lease, a merge in flight, or work that isn't committed and merged. Turned off, idle slots stay until you remove them.
settings.advanced.hive.slots.removeIdle..description: What the advanced setting "Remove idle slots after a day" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane; a lease is one loan of it.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.removeIdle..defaultMessage: Remove idle slots after a day
settings.advanced.hive.slots.removeIdle..description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane and gets back when it ends; free ones are kept ready.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.renameAdopt.defaultMessage: At the upgrade to 1.0 your agents' worktrees became slots, keeping their folders (hb2). Once one is free, with no agent or process in it, Combwork renames its folder to a slot's name (slot-c), moving its cards' work and the agents' conversations with it, so a slot named after one agent isn't lent to another. Turned off, they keep their names.
settings.advanced.hive.slots.renameAdopt.description: What the advanced setting "Rename adopted worktrees to slot names" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane. Keep hb2 and slot-c as they are (folder names).

settings.advanced.hive.slots.renameAdopt.defaultMessage: Rename adopted worktrees to slot names
settings.advanced.hive.slots.renameAdopt.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. At the upgrade to 1.0, agents' own worktrees became slots (worktrees Hive lends to a card or a lane), keeping their folder names.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.setupMinute.defaultMessage: How long Combwork lets a slot's setup command, a dependency install or its archive command run before it ends it. A slot whose setup was ended this way isn't lent until it is set up again; an archive command ended so keeps its slot.
settings.advanced.hive.slots.setupMinute.description: What the advanced setting "Slots: longest a setup command runs" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.setupMinute.defaultMessage: Slots: longest a setup command runs
settings.advanced.hive.slots.setupMinute.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in minutes ("60 min"). A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.allKeysT.defaultMessage: In an agent's pane, Combwork's own shortcuts (Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts) take their keys, apart from those the CLI uses itself. Turned on, every key goes to the CLI, except the command palette's shortcut (Show All Commands), which stays Combwork's so every command is still in reach. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V have their own setting.
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.allKeysT.description: What the advanced setting "All keys go to the CLI" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Show All Commands is a command's name and Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts a place in Hive: use them as Hive shows them. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V name keys.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.allKeysT.defaultMessage: All keys go to the CLI
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.allKeysT.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: every key pressed in an agent's pane goes to its CLI.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.ctrlCVTo.defaultMessage: In an agent's pane, Ctrl+C copies the terminal's selection (with nothing selected it goes to the CLI, which stops what it is doing), and Ctrl+V pastes the clipboard's text, or a screenshot as an attachment. Turned on, both keys go to the CLI, as in any other terminal: copy and paste with right-click instead, unless right-click goes to the CLI too (a setting under each CLI).
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.ctrlCVTo.description: What the advanced setting "Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V go to the CLI" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V name keys: use the key names your language uses.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.ctrlCVTo.defaultMessage: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V go to the CLI
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.ctrlCVTo.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V name keys: use the key names your language uses.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.al.description: A choice of the advanced setting "A CLI putting text on the clipboard": take the text at once.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.as.description: A choice of the advanced setting "A CLI putting text on the clipboard": show the user the text and ask first.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.bl.description: A choice of the advanced setting "A CLI putting text on the clipboard": take none.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.de.defaultMessage: An agent's CLI can put text on the clipboard (OSC 52) just after you press a key or click in its pane, as Copilot does when you copy its own selection. Allow takes it at once; Ask each time shows you the text first, to copy or not; Block takes none. A CLI can never read the clipboard, whatever this says.
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.de.description: What the advanced setting "A CLI putting text on the clipboard" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). OSC 52 is the name of a terminal feature: keep it. Allow, Ask each time and Block are the setting's choices: use the words its list shows.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.ti.defaultMessage: A CLI putting text on the clipboard
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.ti.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: what Hive does when an agent's CLI asks to set the clipboard (OSC 52).

settings.advanced.hive.usage.timelineDet.defaultMessage: How long the usage history keeps when each request happened, to the second, after a session ends. Past it, a session's use over time is kept in 1-hour steps, so the history stays small. Totals, tokens and costs stay exact; only where a card's or lane's share began or ended inside an hour is less exact, for sessions that old.
settings.advanced.hive.usage.timelineDet.description: What the advanced setting "Usage history: keep full detail for" does, and what is lost past it (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A lane is a card loop: a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn.

settings.advanced.hive.usage.timelineDet.defaultMessage: Usage history: keep full detail for
settings.advanced.hive.usage.timelineDet.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in days ("14 days"). The usage history is the record Hive keeps of what each session used.

settings.advanced.hive.wait.agentsMaxSec.defaultMessage: The longest cw_wait_for_agents waits for agents to finish before it answers. Kept a minute below Codex's hive tool timeout, as card waits are.
settings.advanced.hive.wait.agentsMaxSec.description: What the advanced setting "Agent waits: longest" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.wait.cardMaxSecon.defaultMessage: The longest an agent's cw_wait_for_tasks call (without wake) waits before it answers. It has to stay under the CLIs' own tool timeouts, so Combwork keeps it a minute below Codex's hive tool timeout whatever is set here.
settings.advanced.hive.wait.cardMaxSecon.description: What the advanced setting "Card waits: longest" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.workflow.enforce..defaultMessage: Combwork keeps each project's workflow rules as cards move: what its Version Control options ask for before a card reaches Review, Approved or Done, and what follows when Combwork sees a card's work merged or changed outside Combwork. Turned off, every rule is off at once in every project: cards move wherever they are put, nothing is refused or asked, and Combwork only records what happens to each card's work, without moving cards or waking agents for it.
settings.advanced.hive.workflow.enforce..description: What the advanced setting "Workflow rules are enforced" does, and what turning it off does (Settings → Advanced). Version Control is the name of a tab in Project Settings, and Review, Approved and Done are board stages: use them as Hive shows them.

An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. The workflow rules are the checks a card passes as it moves across the board (review, checks, merging), set per project in its Version Control options.

settings.advanced.hive.workflow.updateAg.defaultMessage: When a card from an agent's own worktree was squashed into its target, the agent's branch still has its commits, so its next card in the lane would include them. On, Combwork moves the branch to the target before the next card starts, once the agent is idle, its runs have ended and its worktree is clean, and only when everything on it is in the target: anything else, it asks you under For you. Off, Combwork asks you every time: approve to let it move the branch once, or decline and do it yourself. Combwork never moves a branch with workflow rules turned off.
settings.advanced.hive.workflow.updateAg.description: What the advanced setting "Bring an agent's branch up to date after a squash merge" does (Settings → Advanced). For you is the board's list of what waits for the user: use it as Hive shows it.

settings.advanced.hive.workflow.updateAg.defaultMessage: Bring an agent's branch up to date after a squash merge
settings.advanced.hive.workflow.updateAg.description: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. A squash merge puts a card's commits into the target as one new commit, so the agent's own branch (in its worktree) still has the old ones; Hive can move the branch to the target before the agent's next card.

settings.advanced.reset.tip.defaultMessage: Recent workspaces and window position are kept.
settings.advanced.reset.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Reset all settings" (Settings → Advanced): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.advanced.showDeveloperFeatures..description: The info tip of the setting this (Settings → Advanced): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.advanced.values.desc.defaultMessage: Details Combwork relies on that a CLI update can break (the text of its prompts, the fields it sends), and timeouts and limits for power users. Change one only when something doesn't work, or Combwork's notes on a CLI update say to.
settings.advanced.values.desc.description: What the setting "Advanced settings" does, under its title (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.values.tip.defaultMessage: Each shows its default beside it once changed, and Reset puts the default back. A value that isn't valid is ignored, with a warning, and the default used. They are kept in advanced.json in your Combwork profile, which you can also edit by hand (Open advanced.json): Combwork reads it again when it changes. A value for a CLI records the CLI version it was made for, and is flagged when another version is installed. Some take a workspace's own value too.

settings.advancedList.appliesToSessions.description: A line of an advanced value's info tip.

settings.advancedList.inboxAvailableOpen.description: Button in the note on whether agents can read their inbox (Settings → Advanced): shows Settings → Agent API.

settings.advancedList.reset.description: Button beside an advanced value changed from its default: puts it back. {value} is the default.

settings.advancedList.restartDue.description: Under an advanced value that applies when Hive restarts, changed since Hive started.

settings.advancedList.restartFailed.description: An error's title: restarting Hive from Settings → Advanced failed.

settings.agentApi.allowSessionInput.desc.description: What the setting "Allow sending input to sessions" does, under its title (Settings → Agent API).

settings.assistant.compactSuggestTokens..description: The info tip of the setting "Highlight Compact over" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.control.desc.defaultMessage: What the Assistant may do beyond looking and advising, in every workspace.

settings.assistant.control.tip.agents.defaultMessage: Control agents: it can also add agents, change their settings, start and stop them, and give idle ones tasks, when you ask it to. Stopping a busy agent asks you first.
settings.assistant.control.tip.agents.description: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): a line on the choice Control agents.

settings.assistant.control.tip.inbox.defaultMessage: How the Assistant hears of its inbox follows Settings → Advanced's three inbox switches (Tell a working agent at the end of a tool, Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items, Wake an idle agent), Settings' own values: a project's don't apply to it.
settings.assistant.control.tip.inbox.description: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): a paragraph on which inbox switches the Assistant follows. The three names in brackets are settings of Settings → Advanced: use their names as Hive shows them.

settings.assistant.control.tip.look.defaultMessage: Look and advise: it reads and suggests, and you act.

settings.assistant.control.tip.projects.defaultMessage: Control agents and create projects: also new projects.

settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.tip.defaultMessage: Turn this off if you often type a line and then keep writing (e.g. answering a question, then adding more).
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Enter ends the pause" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.journal.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Journal" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.journal.title.description: A setting's title (Settings → Assistant): the Assistant's journal, its memory across sessions.

settings.assistant.mcp.show.description: A button in Settings → Assistant → MCP servers (HI-2059): shows the Hive Assistant's view on the activity bar, where its MCP servers are added.

settings.assistant.mcp.title.description: A setting's title (Settings → Assistant): which of the open workspace's MCP servers the Assistant gets. MCP is a protocol's name: keep it.

settings.assistant.mode.desc.defaultMessage: How the Assistant works in a new conversation (Coordinator, Planner, QA triager, Release manager, or your own), unless a workspace chooses another.
settings.assistant.mode.desc.description: What the setting "Default mode" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.mode.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Default mode" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.panelSide.option.righ.description: A choice of the setting "Panel side" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.panelSide.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Panel side" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.tellReplies.desc.defaultMessage: The Assistant's watch on an agent or its card hears the first line of what you send that agent from its pane.

settings.assistant.tellReplies.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.typingPause.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Pause after you type" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.connection.context.description: Label of a connection's context window choice in its dialog (HI-2107): 1M tokens or 200K.

settings.connections.server.editTitle.description: Title of the dialog changing a server connection's base URL and models ({name}, its name).

settings.connections.server.hostKey.description: A server connection's line in Settings → Accounts & Connections: its server's host, and its key by its last 4 characters ({last4}).

settings.connections.server.hostLocal.description: A server connection's line: its server is on this computer and has no key (none needed).

settings.connections.server.hostNoKey.description: A server connection's line: its server's host, with no key saved.

settings.connections.server.key.description: Label of a server connection's API key box (Settings → Accounts & Connections).

settings.connections.server.keyCleared.defaultMessage: {name}'s server changed, so its key was removed. Add the key for the new server.
settings.connections.server.keyCleared.description: A notice after a server connection was moved to another server ({name}, its name): its old key was deleted.

settings.connections.server.keyFailed.description: An error's title: a server connection's API key wasn't saved (Settings → Accounts & Connections).

settings.connections.server.keyFailedAdd.defaultMessage: {name} was added without its key. Use Add Key on it to try again.
settings.connections.server.keyFailedAdd.description: The error's text when a server connection ({name}) was added but its API key couldn't be stored. Add Key names a button on it.

settings.connections.server.keyHint.defaultMessage: Stored encrypted for your Windows account, never shown again. The agent's commands can read it from their environment.
settings.connections.server.keyHint.description: Under a server connection's API key box: how Hive keeps the key, and that an agent running on it can read it (it is in the agent's environment).

settings.connections.server.keyLocal.defaultMessage: Not needed for a server on this PC.
settings.connections.server.keyLocal.description: Under a server connection's API key box when its base URL is this computer (localhost): the key may be left empty.

settings.connections.server.keySave.description: The confirm button of the dialog asking a server connection's API key.

settings.connections.server.keyTitle.description: Title of the dialog asking a server connection's API key ({name}, its name).

settings.connections.server.local.description: A preset of a server connection that runs on the user's own computer ({name}: "Ollama").

settings.connections.server.modelId.description: Placeholder of a model's id box in a server connection's model list ("deepseek-flash").

settings.connections.server.models.description: Label of a server connection's model list (Settings → Accounts & Connections).

settings.connections.server.modelsHint.defaultMessage: Each Claude name (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) runs the model ticked for it. A model can stand in for several.
settings.connections.server.modelsHint.description: Under a server connection's model list: the CLI asks for Claude models by name, and each name runs the server model ticked for it.

settings.connections.server.moveWarn.defaultMessage: This is another server: its key will be removed, and you add the key for this one after.
settings.connections.server.moveWarn.description: A warning in the dialog changing a server connection's base URL: the new URL is on another server, so the saved key (for the old server) is deleted when it is saved.

settings.connections.server.needUrl.defaultMessage: Give the base URL in full, starting with https:// (or http:// for this PC).
settings.connections.server.needUrl.description: A server connection form's error: the base URL is empty or can't be used.

settings.connections.server.needsKey.defaultMessage: Its server needs a key: agents on it are refused until one is added.
settings.connections.server.needsKey.description: A warning on a server connection with no key whose server isn't on this computer.

settings.connections.server.preset.description: Label of a server connection's preset (Add Connection): a filled form for a known service.

settings.connections.server.read.description: Button on a server connection: reads its models from the server's model list.

settings.connections.server.readAfter.defaultMessage: Read the models from the server once it is added
settings.connections.server.readAfter.description: A tick box in Add Connection for a server: its models are read from the server (its model list) right after it is added.

settings.connections.server.readDone.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {# model read from {name}.} other {# models read from {name}.}}
settings.connections.server.readDone.description: A notice after reading a server connection's models ({name}, its name).

settings.connections.server.readDropped.defaultMessage: No longer listed, so taken out: {models}
settings.connections.server.readDropped.description: A second line of that notice: models the server doesn't list any more, removed from the connection ({models}, their ids).

settings.connections.server.readFailed.description: An error's title: reading a server connection's models failed ({name}, its name).

settings.connections.server.reading.description: A server connection's Read Models button while it reads them.

settings.connections.server.removeKey.description: Button on a server connection with a key: deletes it (asks first).

settings.connections.server.removeKeyMes.defaultMessage: It's deleted from this PC. Agents running on it keep it until they restart; new ones are refused until a key is added.
settings.connections.server.removeKeyMes.description: The message of the dialog confirming a server connection's key is deleted.

settings.connections.server.removeKeyTit.description: Title of the dialog confirming a server connection's key is deleted ({name}, its name).

settings.connections.server.removeModel.description: Tooltip of the button removing a model ({model}, its id) from a server connection's list.

settings.connections.server.replaceKey.description: Button on a server connection with a key: asks for a new one in its place.

settings.connections.server.save.description: The confirm button of the dialog changing a server connection's server.

settings.connections.server.saving.description: A dialog's confirm button in Settings → Accounts & Connections while it saves.

settings.connections.server.setKey.description: Button on a server connection with no key: asks for one.

settings.connections.server.setUp.description: Button on a connection (a server one, or one signed in): opens the CLI on it in a terminal, for its first-run screens (its theme, its notes), answered by the user.

settings.connections.server.setUpFailed.description: An error's title: a connection's Set Up terminal couldn't be opened.

settings.connections.server.why.failed.defaultMessage: The server answered with an error ({status}). Try again later.
settings.connections.server.why.failed.description: Why reading a server connection's models failed: the server answered with an HTTP error. {status} is its code (500).

settings.connections.server.why.forbidde.defaultMessage: The server refused access (403): the key may not be allowed to list models. Type the models in instead.
settings.connections.server.why.forbidde.description: Why reading a server connection's models failed: access was refused, though the key may be fine for using models.

settings.connections.server.why.redirect.defaultMessage: The server sent Combwork elsewhere ({status}), which Combwork doesn't follow with a key. Check the base URL.
settings.connections.server.why.redirect.description: Why reading a server connection's models failed: the server answered with a redirect. {status} is its code (301).

settings.connections.server.why.refused.defaultMessage: The server refused the key (401). Replace the key, then read again.
settings.connections.server.why.refused.description: Why reading a server connection's models failed: its API key was refused.

settings.connections.server.why.shape.defaultMessage: The server's answer isn't a model list Combwork can read. Type the models in instead.
settings.connections.server.why.shape.description: Why reading a server connection's models failed: its reply isn't the list Hive expects.

settings.connections.server.why.stale.defaultMessage: The account changed while its models were read. Read them again.
settings.connections.server.why.stale.description: Why reading a server connection's models was dropped: its server or key changed meanwhile, or a newer reading started.

settings.connections.server.why.tooBig.defaultMessage: The model list is too large to read. Type the models in instead.
settings.connections.server.why.tooBig.description: Why reading a server connection's models failed: its reply was over Hive's size limit.

settings.connections.server.why.unreacha.defaultMessage: Couldn't reach the server: check its base URL and that it is running.
settings.connections.server.why.unreacha.description: Why reading a server connection's models failed: no answer (not running, wrong address, a timeout).

settings.data.copied.description: A notice after a path was copied.

settings.data.copyPath.description: Button beside the settings file's path (Settings → Advanced → Settings file): copies it.

settings.emptyDefault.description: In "Reset to default (empty)": the setting's default is empty.

settings.enable.description: Button of the confirmation before a risky setting is turned on.

settings.fallback.add.description: Button under a fallback list: adds the value typed beside it.

settings.fallback.level.description: A column of a provider's fallback list of effort levels: the value Hive passes to the CLI.

settings.fallback.levelPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the box where a new effort level is typed. xhigh is a level's value: keep it.

settings.fallback.levelsPerModel.defaultMessage: {source}: each model offers its own levels; this list names them and is used for models it doesn't describe.
settings.fallback.levelsPerModel.description: Above a provider's fallback list of effort levels, when the CLI reports each model's levels. {source} says where the models come from.

settings.fallback.levelsUsed.defaultMessage: Used now: {provider} hasn't reported per-model levels.
settings.fallback.levelsUsed.description: Above a provider's fallback list of effort levels, when the CLI reports none per model. {provider} is its name.

settings.fallback.modelId.description: A column of a provider's fallback list of models: the ID Hive passes to the CLI.

settings.fallback.modelsNow.description: Above a provider's fallback list of models: where the model pickers' models come from now. {source} says it.

settings.fallback.name.description: A column of a provider's fallback list: the name pickers show.

settings.fallback.nameCell.description: The name, for screen readers, of a row's Name box in a fallback list. {n} is the row's number.

settings.fallback.newLevel.description: The name, for screen readers, of the box under a fallback list of effort levels where a new one is typed.

settings.fallback.newModel.description: The name, for screen readers, of the box under a fallback list of models where a new one is typed.

settings.fallback.older.description: A column of a provider's fallback list of models: ticked, the model is listed under Older models.

settings.fallback.olderCell.description: The name, for screen readers, of a row's Older box in a fallback list. {n} is the row's number.

settings.fallback.remove.description: Button on a row of a fallback list: removes it.

settings.fallback.reset.description: Button under a provider's table (prices, models or effort levels): goes back to Hive's own.

settings.fallback.saveFailed.description: An error's title: saving a provider's fallback list of models or effort levels failed.

settings.fallback.showLevels.defaultMessage: Show the list ({n, plural, one {# level} other {# levels}})
settings.fallback.showLevels.description: A link that unfolds a provider's fallback list of effort levels. {n} is how many it holds.

settings.fallback.showModels.defaultMessage: Show the list ({n, plural, one {# model} other {# models}})
settings.fallback.showModels.description: A link that unfolds a provider's fallback list of models. {n} is how many it holds.

settings.fallback.valueCell.description: The name, for screen readers, of a box in a fallback list: the column and the row's number.

settings.general.closeToTray.desc.defaultMessage: Closing the window keeps Combwork running in the system tray so sessions continue.
settings.general.closeToTray.desc.description: What the setting "Close to tray" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.closeToTray.tip.defaultMessage: When off, closing the window quits Combwork (asking first if sessions are running). Use File → Exit or the tray menu to quit.
settings.general.closeToTray.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Close to tray" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.commands.desc.defaultMessage: Your own commands for Combwork as a whole: run one by hand (here, or Run Command in the command palette), or pick them for When Combwork quits, run, or for any workspace's open and close.
settings.general.commands.desc.description: What the setting "Commands" does, under its title (Settings → General, HI-1954). When Hive quits, run is another setting's title: use its translation.

settings.general.commands.tip.defaultMessage: Saved in Combwork's own settings, never in a workspace, so a repository you clone brings none that run by themselves. Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.general.commands.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Commands" (Settings → General, HI-1954).

settings.general.commands.title.description: A setting's title (Settings → General): the user's own named commands for Hive as a whole (HI-1954).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.desc.defaultMessage: When to ask before quitting stops running sessions.
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.desc.description: What the setting "Confirm before quitting" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.option.al.description: A choice of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.option.ne.description: A choice of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.option.wo.description: A choice of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.tip.defaultMessage: Quitting stops every running session. Their conversations are kept and can be resumed, so by default Combwork only asks when an agent is in the middle of something (working, or waiting for your answer).
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.dateFormat.desc.defaultMessage: How dates show in Combwork: sessions named by when they started, the session lists and their tooltips, exports.
settings.general.dateFormat.desc.description: What the setting "Date format" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.dmy.description: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.mdy.description: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.syste.description: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.ymd.description: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.tip.defaultMessage: System uses your Windows language's short date. Names you give sessions stay as you typed them: only the automatic ones (when a session started) follow this. How long ago something happened ("2 hours ago") stays, with the date on hover.
settings.general.dateFormat.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.keepAwake.desc.defaultMessage: Stop Windows from sleeping while an agent is working or waiting on background tasks, so it doesn't stop mid-task.
settings.general.keepAwake.desc.description: What the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.option.always.description: A choice of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.option.never.description: A choice of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.option.plugge.description: A choice of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.tip.defaultMessage: Combwork lets the PC sleep again as soon as no agent is working. The screen can still turn off and lock. On a laptop, "When plugged in" lets it sleep on battery.
settings.general.keepAwake.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.keepAwake.title.defaultMessage: Keep the PC awake while agents work

settings.general.launchAtLogin.desc.defaultMessage: Start Combwork automatically when you sign in to Windows.
settings.general.launchAtLogin.desc.description: What the setting "Launch at login" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.launchAtLogin.tip.defaultMessage: Combwork starts hidden in the tray when launched at login.
settings.general.launchAtLogin.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Launch at login" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.minimizeToTray.desc.defaultMessage: Minimising hides Combwork to the system tray instead of the taskbar.
settings.general.minimizeToTray.desc.description: What the setting "Minimise to tray" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.minimizeToTray.tip.defaultMessage: Click the tray icon to bring Combwork back.
settings.general.minimizeToTray.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Minimise to tray" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.onQuit.desc.defaultMessage: The commands Combwork runs, in order, as it quits, once every window's workspace has closed. Combwork waits for them, showing them running.
settings.general.onQuit.desc.description: What the setting "When Hive quits, run" does, under its title (Settings → General; HI-1954: a list of the user's commands).

settings.general.onQuit.tip.defaultMessage: Pick them from Commands above. '{reason}' becomes quit, or update when Combwork restarts to install an update (only with that box ticked). Don't wait, in the dialog Combwork shows, lets Combwork go on while the rest run by themselves. Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.general.onQuit.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "When Hive quits, run" (Settings → General; HI-1954). '{reason}' is a placeholder the user writes in a command, and quit and update are the values it becomes: keep all three as they are (the quotes around {reason} keep it from being read as a placeholder of this text). Commands is the title of the setting above; Don't wait is the name of a button of the dialog.

settings.general.onQuit.title.description: A setting's title (Settings → General): a command of the user's that Hive runs as it quits.

settings.general.progressCommands.desc.defaultMessage: Agents run tests, builds and other commands that take more than about 30 seconds through hive-progress without being asked, so they show in the panel. Off: only when you ask.
settings.general.progressCommands.desc.description: What the setting "Agents show long commands in the Progress panel" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.progressCommands.disabl.defaultMessage: Turn on the Progress panel to use this.
settings.general.progressCommands.disabl.description: Under the setting "Agents show long commands in the Progress panel" (Settings → General) while the Progress panel is off.

settings.general.progressCommands.tip.defaultMessage: hive-progress runs the command unchanged (same output and exit code). Combwork's session guidance tells agents to use it, so a change applies to agents started or restarted afterwards. With the Progress panel off, agents aren't told to use it either.
settings.general.progressCommands.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Agents show long commands in the Progress panel" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.progressCommands.title.defaultMessage: Agents show long commands in the Progress panel

settings.general.progressPanel.desc.defaultMessage: Show long runs agents report, such as tests and builds: how far along each is and the time left, in a panel on the right and on the taskbar button.
settings.general.progressPanel.desc.description: What the setting "Progress panel" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.progressPanel.tip.defaultMessage: Folded, the panel is a strip with a small bar per run; click it, or use Toggle Progress Panel in the command palette. Off hides the panel, the strip and the taskbar progress; agents can still report, and Combwork ignores it.
settings.general.progressPanel.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Progress panel" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.des.defaultMessage: Open the workspace you used last when Combwork starts.
settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.des.description: What the setting "Reopen last workspace" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.tip.defaultMessage: Sessions are never resumed automatically — only the workspace is reopened.
settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Reopen last workspace" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.showTips.desc.defaultMessage: One tip a day about something Combwork can do, and a tip at the moments one helps.
settings.general.showTips.desc.description: What the setting "Show a tip when Hive starts" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.showTips.tip.defaultMessage: Tips show in a small card in the bottom corner and never get in the way. Help → Tips… lists them all, whether this is on or off.
settings.general.showTips.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Show a tip when Hive starts" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.showTips.title.defaultMessage: Show a tip when Combwork starts

settings.general.startMinimized.desc.defaultMessage: Start Combwork hidden in the system tray.
settings.general.startMinimized.desc.description: What the setting "Start in tray" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.startMinimized.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Start in tray" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.timeFormat.desc.defaultMessage: How times show with the dates.
settings.general.timeFormat.desc.description: What the setting "Time format" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.timeFormat.option.12h.description: A choice of the setting "Time format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.timeFormat.option.24h.description: A choice of the setting "Time format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.timeFormat.tip.defaultMessage: Applies wherever Combwork shows a time, such as a session that started today or the time a screenshot was pasted.
settings.general.timeFormat.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Time format" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.userName.desc.defaultMessage: How Combwork names you to the Assistant when it tells it you replied to an agent ("Darren replied to B1 on #399").
settings.general.userName.desc.description: What the setting "Your name" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.userName.placeholder.description: The empty box's placeholder of the setting "Your name" (Settings → General).

settings.general.userName.tip.defaultMessage: It goes into the Assistant's conversation, so use whatever form you like it to see. Empty uses "User".
settings.general.userName.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Your name" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.journal.cap.description: A label before the journal's size limit in MB (Settings → Assistant → Journal).

settings.journal.days.description: After the number of days everyday journal entries are kept.

settings.journal.delete.description: A button: deletes the Assistant's journal of this workspace (asks first). The … says it asks: keep it.

settings.journal.deleteButton.description: Button of the confirmation: deletes the journal.

settings.journal.deleteMessage.defaultMessage: All {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} of this workspace go to the Recycle Bin. The Assistant starts again with an empty journal.
settings.journal.deleteMessage.description: The question before the journal is deleted; {entries} is how many entries it has. Recycle Bin is Windows' name for it.

settings.journal.deleteTitle.description: Title of the question before the Assistant's journal is deleted.

settings.journal.deleted.description: A notice after the Assistant's journal was deleted.

settings.journal.failed.description: An error's title: saving the journal settings or deleting the journal failed (why follows).

settings.journal.kind.decision.description: A kind of entry the Assistant may keep in its journal (Settings → Assistant → Journal): what was decided.

settings.journal.kind.event.description: A kind of journal entry: what happened (Hive records lanes, merges and unexpected closes as events too).

settings.journal.kind.incident.description: A kind of journal entry: something that went wrong.

settings.journal.kind.insight.description: A kind of journal entry: something learned.

settings.journal.kind.moment.description: A kind of journal entry: a memorable moment of working together. Off by default.

settings.journal.kind.plan.description: A kind of journal entry: what is planned.

settings.journal.kind.preference.description: A kind of journal entry: how the user likes things done. Off by default.

settings.journal.local.defaultMessage: Kept on this computer only, in .hive/assistant/journal.db, and never sent anywhere.
settings.journal.local.description: A note under the journal settings (privacy). Keep the file path as it is.

settings.journal.mb.defaultMessage: MB (past it, the oldest everyday entries go first)
settings.journal.mb.description: After the journal's size limit in megabytes.

settings.journal.noLimit.description: A checkbox: the journal has no size limit.

settings.journal.noWorkspace.defaultMessage: Open a workspace to set its Assistant's journal.
settings.journal.noWorkspace.description: Settings → Assistant → Journal with no workspace open.

settings.journal.none.description: The journal before the Assistant or Hive has written anything.

settings.journal.offKeeps.defaultMessage: Off, nothing is written and the Assistant's journal tools go at its next start; the entries are kept.
settings.journal.offKeeps.description: Under the journal switch when it is off.

settings.journal.on.description: A switch (Settings → Assistant → Journal): the Assistant keeps a journal in this workspace. Off keeps what is there.

settings.journal.retention.description: A label before a number of days (Settings → Assistant → Journal). Digests and important entries are kept longer.

settings.journal.scope.description: A heading (Settings → Assistant → Journal): the kinds of entries the Assistant may keep.

settings.journal.size.defaultMessage: Now {size}, {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}.
settings.journal.size.description: The journal's size on disk ({size}: "1.2 MB") and how many entries it has.

settings.keybindings.editor.desc.defaultMessage: Click the pencil (or double-click a shortcut), then press the new keys. Wait a moment after the first combination, or press a second one for a chord such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+S.
settings.keybindings.editor.desc.description: What the setting "Shortcuts" does, under its title (Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts).

settings.keybindings.editor.tip.defaultMessage: Shortcuts need Ctrl or Alt (or are F-keys). Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Shift+Tab stay with editing and the agents' terminals. Some keys go to the agent while its terminal has focus (for Claude Code: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+G).
settings.keybindings.editor.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Shortcuts" (Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.keys.all.description: The keyboard shortcuts editor's first tab: every command, of every category. Short.

settings.keys.alsoUsed.description: Tooltip of the warning beside a shortcut other commands use too. {commands} lists them.

settings.keys.cantUse.description: Title of a warning when a recorded shortcut can't be used. {keys} is the shortcut (Ctrl+K).

settings.keys.change.description: Button on a command's row of the shortcuts editor: records a new shortcut.

settings.keys.chordNext.defaultMessage: then another key for a chord…
settings.keys.chordNext.description: While a shortcut is recorded, after its first key combination: press a second one for a chord (such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+S).

settings.keys.column.category.description: A column of the keyboard shortcuts editor: the command's category (Project, Session…).

settings.keys.column.command.description: A column of the keyboard shortcuts editor: the command.

settings.keys.column.set.description: A column of the keyboard shortcuts editor: where the shortcut comes from (changed, removed, this project…). Keep it short.

settings.keys.column.shortcut.description: A column of the keyboard shortcuts editor: the keys.

settings.keys.commandIn.description: A command named with its category, where it may be on another tab of the shortcuts editor (Also used by…, Shortcut already in use): "Session: Compact Conversation". Keep the order natural for the language.

settings.keys.inUseDetail.defaultMessage: When two commands share a shortcut, the first one listed that is available runs. Change the other one to avoid surprises.
settings.keys.inUseDetail.description: More in the question when a recorded shortcut is already used.

settings.keys.inUseMessage.defaultMessage: {keys} is used by {commands}. Use it here too?
settings.keys.inUseMessage.description: The question when a recorded shortcut is already used. {keys} is the shortcut; {commands} lists the commands using it.

settings.keys.inUseTitle.description: Title of the question when a recorded shortcut is already used by another command.

settings.keys.noMatch.description: The keyboard shortcuts editor when its search finds nothing.

settings.keys.press.description: While a shortcut is recorded, before any key. <faint> marks the part shown greyed; Esc is a key: keep it.

settings.keys.projectNote.defaultMessage: Changes here apply while {project} is selected, over the global shortcuts. Other commands are set in Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts.
settings.keys.projectNote.description: Above a project's shortcuts (Project Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts). {project} is its name.

settings.keys.remove.description: Button on a command's row of the shortcuts editor: removes its shortcut.

settings.keys.reset.description: Button of the question before shortcuts go back to their defaults.

settings.keys.resetAll.description: Button of the keyboard shortcuts editor: every changed shortcut goes back.

settings.keys.resetAllGlobal.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {Return # changed shortcut to the defaults.} other {Return # changed shortcuts to the defaults.}}
settings.keys.resetAllGlobal.description: The question before every changed shortcut goes back to its default (Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts). {n} is how many.

settings.keys.resetAllProject.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {Remove {project}'s shortcut change; it uses the global shortcuts again.} other {Remove {project}'s # shortcut changes; it uses the global shortcuts again.}}
